title: Canonical unit, tensor, dual and tower maps for scalar extension
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site with topology $J$, and let $R\xrightarrow{\alpha}S\xrightarrow{\beta}T$ be sheaves of commutative rings. Use the actual sheaf tensor, scalar-extension sections, and module sheafification of [def-sp-scalar-tensor-comparison-data], and the slice internal Hom of [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Use a coefficient universe $u$ independent of the two site universes, and module sheaves in $u$ for the unit, binary and internal-dual input constructions. Internal Hom has universe $\max(u_{\mathcal C},v_{\mathcal C},u)$. Assume sheafification and its locally bijective characterization in the coefficient, module and internal-Hom universes used below, and on slices as needed for internal Hom; the object and morphism universes of the site are independent. Write $E_\alpha M=M\otimes_R S$, with the scalar-first section convention $s\otimes x$. Define the following existing canonical maps by the balanced section formulas descended through module sheafification. The unit isomorphism $u_\alpha:E_\alpha R\simeq S$ sends $s\otimes r$ to $s\alpha(r)$. For arbitrary $R$-module sheaves $M,N$, the binary isomorphism $\sigma_\alpha:E_\alpha(M\otimes_R N)\simeq E_\alpha M\otimes_S E_\alpha N$ sends $s\otimes(x\otimes y)$ to $(s\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$, with inverse $(s\otimes x)\otimes(t\otimes y)\mapsto st\otimes(x\otimes y)$. For arbitrary $M$, the internal-dual morphism $d_{\alpha,M}:E_\alpha\mathcal Hom_R(M,R)\to\mathcal Hom_S(E_\alpha M,S)$ sends $s\otimes\varphi$ to the slice functional $t\otimes x\mapsto st\alpha(\varphi(x))$. It is a morphism, without any assertion here that it is invertible. Finally, for every module sheaf $M$ in a universe containing the coefficient universe, define the tower isomorphism $A_{\alpha,\beta,M}:E_\beta E_\alpha M\simeq E_{\alpha\gg\beta}M$ by $t\otimes(s\otimes x)\mapsto(t\beta(s))\otimes x$, with inverse $t\otimes x\mapsto t\otimes(1\otimes x)$. These definitions require neither flatness nor local freeness.
